html:
The Nuwuvi, or Southern Paiute, are a Numic people of the Colorado Plateau and Mojave Desert, in today's southern Utah, southern Nevada, northern Arizona and southeastern California. Their language belongs to the Uto-Aztecan family, close to those of the Ute and the Chemehuevi.

They lived in small bands, gathering pine nuts, seeds and agave and hunting rabbits and bighorn sheep; many also farmed maize and squash beside springs and streams. From the late 1700s Ute and New Mexican raiders along the Old Spanish Trail seized Paiute children and sold them as slaves. Mormon settlers arrived in the 1850s and took the best water. In 1857 Mormon militiamen, with some Paiute men they had recruited, killed about 120 emigrants in the Mountain Meadows massacre, then blamed the Paiutes alone. Today they belong to several small tribes, such as the Kaibab and Moapa bands. The map shows them in later centuries as Southern Paiute.
